mexican-chicken-rice.style: standard US + AU terms + metric can
lines: 2 tsp garlic powder (or 2 garlic cloves, minced)
5 chicken thighs, bone-in, skin on (Notes 2 and 3)
1 small onion , peeled and diced (or 1/2 large)
1 red capsicum (bell pepper), diced or sliced
1 cup chicken stock/broth , low sodium (or vegetable stock)
1 cup frozen corn kernels (or canned - drained)
1 can (400g/16oz) black beans , drained and rinsed (sub red kidney beans)

cauliflower-tacos.style: dotted units, divided, inch prep, purpose lines
lines: 1 large head cauliflower, cut into 2" florets
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for serving
2 Tbsp. freshly sliced chives, plus more for garnish
2 Tbsp. freshly chopped parsley, plus more for garnish
1/4 tsp. kosher salt, plus more for seasoning
Pinch of crushed red pepper flakes

ricotta-meatballs.style: raw paste incl. page chrome + headings + essay parentheticals
lines: 1 lb. ground turkey (I used 93/7 ground turkey - ground chicken also works, as does just about any other type of ground meat that you like!)
1 jar tomato sauce (like a marinara or pasta sauce - I like a lot of sauce so I typically use a 28-32 ounce jar)
2 Bone-in Ribeye Steaks: At least 1.5 inches thick (don't skimp here, get the good stuff from the butcher counter).
1 tbsp Kosher salt: Diamond Crystal if you have it.
1 tbsp Coarse black pepper: Freshly cracked.
1/2 tbsp Garlic powder: The secret weapon for a savory crust.

grandma-fried-chicken.style: articles as qty, hedges, folk units, 3-way needs
lines: A whole chicken, cut into pieces (about 3 or 4 pounds)
A scoop of flour, maybe half a cup
A big spoonful of bacon drippings (or butter if you're out)
About a cup of hot spiced apple cider (A lot of folks tell you to use vinegar for this part, but the hot cider is the real secret-it makes the gravy rich and sweet instead of sour)

city-chicken.style: equipment line, 3-way conjunction w/ one amount, glug
lines: 1 pound of pork shoulder, cut into chunky squares
An egg, beaten up in a shallow bowl
A cup of your organic whole wheat high-protein flour (it gives a much better, nuttier crust on these than the cheap bleached stuff anyway)
Salt, pepper, and a heavy pinch of paprika
A good glug of vegetable oil for frying
A mess of fresh-caught bluegill, scaled, gutted, and washed clean (Leave the tails on!)
A good handful of yellow cornmeal
A big scoop of bacon grease or lard (vegetable oil works if that's all you have, but it won't taste nearly as good)
A lemon or a bottle of hot sauce for the table

halloumi-bean-stew.style: UK comma-less: 400g can, half x 250g block, double coriander
lines: 3 tbsp red chilli pesto sundried tomato pesto or vegan alternative
400g can mixed beans drained and rinsed
½ small bunch of coriander finely chopped
½ small red onion, thinly sliced
2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint, plus more to garnish
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
